content.title: Affordable Housing Inventory
content.summary: Affordable Homeownership in Arvada refers to homes sold at prices ensuring that mortgage payments and utilities do not exceed 30% of a household's income, with income limits typically capped at 80% or 100% of the Area Median Income (AMI). The city has 23 income-restricted properties funded by various government sources, aimed at supporting middle and working-class families by providing affordable housing options that promote financial stability. Eligibility for these units is determined by verifying household income against established thresholds based on AMI, which varies according to household size.
content.body:
## What is "Affordable Homeownership"?

Affordable Homeownership is where homes are sold at a price where the mortgage payment plus utilities is estimated to be no more than 30% of the household’s income. Income limits also apply to Affordable Homeownership opportunities. Buyer income is usually capped at either 80% AMI or 100% AMI.

The City of Arvada currently has 23 affordable (income-restricted) properties in its total housing stock. These units were built using Federal, State and Local money, and are under income restrictions as a condition of accepting these funds. The City does not own or manage these properties, but offers support and partnership where appropriate.

To be eligible to live in one of these properties, the tenant’s household income must be below a certain amount. The rent for these units is aligned to income, so that the unit is “affordable” to the tenants. The United States Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) defines an “affordable” home, as one where the occupant spends no more than 30% of their gross income on housing costs.

## Why is Affordable and WorkForce Housing Important to a community?

Aligning rent to income to make sure housing is “affordable” is an extremely important and impactful way to support middle class and working class families in the community. Having an “affordable” housing payment allows the household to save money for emergencies or big purchases, pay down debt, invest in higher education, have some disposable income to spend in the local economy, and achieve general financial stability. The purpose of subsidizing housing with Federal, State, and Local dollars is to make sure households that earn less money still have access to housing options that are “affordable” and do not create financial and housing instability in communities. These income-aligned units are known as Affordable Housing, or WorkForce Housing (though WorkForce Housing targets a slightly higher income).

## Who can live in Affordable and WorkForce Housing?

To determine if a household is eligible to live in an Affordable or WorkForce unit a landlord would verify the new tenant’s income to make sure that it fell below the threshold mandated by the Federal, State, and Local funds used to construct or rehabilitate the property.

Affordable and WorkForce housing income thresholds are based off of Adam’s and Jefferson County’s Area Median Income(s). Area median income (AMI) is the income at which half of all households in the area earn more money, and half earn less. Different Affordable and WorkForce Housing programs target different income levels based off a percentage of AMI.

AMI can be adjusted based on household size. Larger households can have higher income and still qualify to live in an Affordable or WorkForce housing unit.

As of April 1, 2025, the Income Limits for Adams and Jefferson County were as follows:

To live in a unit for a designated income-aligned rent, the household must earn equal to or less than the AMI Limit, however, if a unit is designated for a certain income and the household earns less, the rent will not be adjusted downwards.

### What does this mean? An Example

John and Jane Doe are a married couple living and working in Arvada and have two children. John earns $45,000 per year and Jane earns $55,000 per year, for a total household income of $100,000 per year. For a family of 4, the income limit for an Affordable property is 80% AMI or $112,080. This means that the Doe family is eligible to live in an Affordable housing apartment with rent aligned to 80% AMI or less. The Doe family may rent an Affordable two bedroom apartment for $2,522 or a three bedroom apartment for $2,915.
